Evelyn / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call earlier — super helpful to walk through Redwood's runtime options. Quick recap from our side so we're aligned on constraints and asks before the POC.

Key performance targets we need to validate:
- Sustained throughput: ~800 req/s (conversational API requests) for baseline loads.
- Burst concurrency: spikes up to ~3,000 concurrent requests for 10-15m windows.
- Latency targets: sub-150ms median for short (single-turn) responses; p95 ideally <500ms, p99 <1s for non-streaming; streaming partials tolerated but end-to-end should meet p95 <750ms where possible.
- Streaming: real-time partial responses matter for our chat UX (we stream tokens as they arrive).

Typical payload composition (average):
- System + persona prompt: ~1,800 tokens (fixed)
- Recent user history: ~600 tokens
- Expected model output: 500-900 tokens (varies by flow)
=> Total input+output envelope frequently in the 3k+ token range; we'd like to validate a 4,000 token working window.

Two operational levers we discussed that are high priority for us to test in the POC:
1) Prefetching / KV prewarm — preloading recent convo KV and prefix segments to cut first-token latency for hot users. We think a per-request prefetch budget of ~256 tokens might cover most cases.
2) Fallback / small-model path — during extreme bursts, route to a quantized smaller model (fast, cheaper) that can still stream partials and produce safe responses.

Attachment: preftech-ops-profile.csv (ops profile + sample QPS timeline) — included a few RPS spikes so you can size batching/caching heuristics.

Next steps we need from Redwood:
- Confirmation that KV prewarm with a 256-token prefetch budget is implementable without large cold-start costs.
- A proposed POC configuration (instance types, target number of GPUs, canary plan, and tentative SLA measurements you will collect).
- Pricing/commit guidance for a 2-week dedicated POC.

Happy to share anonymized conversation logs if that helps with synthetic load tests — let me know the preferred upload method.

Thanks,
Alex Wong
Head of Engineering
Prefetch.ai

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the ops profile. Great signal and we'll use that for sizing. Quick responses to the three asks and proposed actions: 

1) KV prewarm / prefetch budget
- Feasible: we can prefetch a per-request prefix of ~256 tokens and keep it in a hot cache attached to the serving shard. Prefetch costs are predictable (we'll show token delta in the POC metrics). For spikes we also support proactive prewarming for cohorts identified by your session IDs.

2) Fallback path
- We recommend a two-tier fallback: a quantized 4B candidate for marginal latency relief, and an even smaller 1.3B policy for severe overloads. Both can stream partial tokens. We'll instrument quality regressions with our eval harness so you can see delta vs. primary model.

3) POC configuration & measurements
- Proposal (tentative): 8x A100 equivalent GPUs in a Redwood Dedicated pool for a 2-week run. We'll measure: median, p95, p99 token-latency, token throughput, cache hit-rate, and end-to-end streaming startup time. We'll also run synthetic burst tests (3k concurrency windows) and a steady-state run at ~800 req/s.
- Default latency hedges: enable 256-token prefetch, enable KV cache TTL=30s for hot sessions, and configure fallback thresholds at 80% GPU utilization / 600ms p95.
- We'll provide a POC runbook and an SLA matrix document for review.

Action items (proposed):
- Redwood: deliver a POC proposal & price by EOD Wed (I attached an SLA matrix draft).
- Prefetch: confirm dates for a 2-week POC window and whether you'll provide anonymized logs or prefer a secure upload.
- Both: decide on success criteria (suggested: sustain 800 req/s with p95 <500ms for primary model and seamless fallback with quality delta <15% on key prompts).

Cc'ing Marissa to loop in deal ops and pricing.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
